challenges.name: Clean Load
challenges.note: No corrections anywhere in the load

challenges.name: Steady Cycle
challenges.note: Held the washer and the sterilizer the whole cycle, first try

hazards.dirty-clean-crossover: That case cart is parked touching the clean assembly bench. The whole point of a decontamination area and a clean assembly area is that nothing contaminated ever touches a surface on the clean side — park it back on the dirty side before anything else moves.
hazards.flash-sterilize-shortcut: That control skips straight to an immediate-use cycle on a tray that hasn't even been counted yet. Immediate-use steam sterilization is an exception for a specific, unplanned need, not a shortcut around decontamination and assembly whenever someone's in a hurry — and it is never a call this bench makes alone.
hazards.unlabeled-tray-decoy: That tray on the clean side has no count sheet and no tracking label on it. An unlabeled tray can't be matched to the case it's going to or the cycle that's supposed to sterilize it — it's untraceable the moment it leaves this bench.
hazards.wrong-size-pouch: That pouch is stuffed and bulging around the tray inside it. A wrap or pouch has to fit the load without crushing the pack — steam needs room to reach every surface, and a pack this crushed hasn't got it.

interrupts.alert: The OR calls down: a case is starting and someone's asking if this tray can be rushed through on immediate-use sterilization instead of the normal line.
interrupts.cue: That is not a call to make alone at this bench.
interrupts.missNote: A rushed tray went up without anyone with the authority to approve it actually signing off. Every step it skipped between here and the OR is now riding on a case already in progress.
interrupts.why: Immediate-use sterilization exists for the case nobody could have planned around, decided under the department's own written policy — not a favor this bench hands out because a room upstairs is waiting, and skipping the decontamination and assembly already underway is not this tech's decision to make solo.
interrupts.wrongNote: Put the call through to the supervisor first — a request like this doesn't get answered from the bench.

interrupts.alert: The sterilizer throws a fault code and stops mid-cycle. The door stays locked.
interrupts.cue: Nothing inside that chamber right now counts as sterile.
interrupts.missNote: The faulted load sat behind a locked door with nobody logging what happened. Whoever opens that chamber next has no way to tell a stopped cycle from a finished one just by looking.
interrupts.why: A chamber that faults out partway through never delivered the full exposure this tray was loaded for — clearing the fault and sending the whole load through again from the start is the only way to know what actually reached it, rather than trusting however far a broken run happened to get.
interrupts.wrongNote: Clear the fault and requeue the whole tray — a chamber that stopped partway doesn't get trusted for however far it got.

lateNotes.record-load: Hold that. The log isn't ready until the sterilizer cycle and the biological indicator are both read.
lateNotes.sterilizer-printout: No cycle is running yet to read a printout from.

name: Sterile Processing Decon & Assembly

passRule.note: stars >= 2 and no unsafe action (WebXR/shared/records.js passed())

steps.cue: Fluid-resistant gown, gloves to the elbow, mask and full face or eye protection before the case cart is opened.
steps.prompt: Fluid-resistant gown, gloves to the elbow, mask and full face or eye protection before the case cart is opened.
steps.title: Don decontamination PPE
steps.why: OSHA's bloodborne pathogens standard treats the decontamination area as a splash zone — a washer's spray arms and a manual pre-soak both throw contaminated fluid, and PPE rated for that is what stands between this job and a mucous-membrane exposure nobody saw coming.

steps.cue: Log the case cart in at the decontamination intake, never past the line into the clean assembly area.
steps.prompt: Log the case cart in at the decontamination intake, never past the line into the clean assembly area.
steps.title: Receive the case cart on the dirty side only
steps.why: The dirty side and the clean side of this department exist because nothing contaminated is allowed to cross back over a clean surface — every tray in this cart is treated as contaminated until it has been all the way through the line.

steps.cue: Take multi-part instruments apart and open every hinge and box lock fully.

itemNames.open-box-locks: open every box lock and hinge

steps.prompt: Take multi-part instruments apart and open every hinge and box lock fully.
steps.title: Disassemble and open before cleaning
steps.why: A hinge closed during cleaning is a hinge the washer's spray never actually reaches — CDC guidance is explicit that instruments are cleaned open and disassembled, because a closed box lock hides exactly the debris a closed inspection would miss too.

steps.cue: Two instruments on this tray need attention before they go anywhere near the washer. Find them.

itemNotes.clogged-lumen: A lumen this blocked never gets an actual wash through its channel — it needs a manual flush before the washer, not a cycle that assumes the channel is already clear.
itemNotes.retained-tissue: Dried tissue sitting in an opened hinge — organic material like this can shield anything underneath it from a washer's spray the same way it shields a load from steam later on.

steps.prompt: Two instruments on this tray need attention before they go anywhere near the washer. Find them.
steps.title: Check for bioburden a washer alone won't clear
steps.why: A washer-disinfector cleans what water and enzymatic detergent can reach — gross bioburden in a hinge or a blocked lumen needs a hand and a brush first, because a machine cycle run over debris this size does not remove it, it just wets it.

steps.cue: Soak and manually brush lumened and hinged instruments in enzymatic solution mixed to the label's dilution, for the label's soak time.
steps.prompt: Soak and manually brush lumened and hinged instruments in enzymatic solution mixed to the label's dilution, for the label's soak time.
steps.title: Pre-soak lumened and hinged instruments
steps.why: Enzymatic detergent breaks down protein bioburden before it dries any harder onto the instrument, and its dilution and soak time are set by its own label — too weak or too short and it's done nothing; the point is contact, per the label, not a quick dip.

steps.cue: Rack the trays open-side down and hold the load through the full washer cycle.
steps.holdBreakNote: The cycle was interrupted before it finished. A partial wash cycle leaves debris the spray arms never got the time to reach.
steps.prompt: Rack the trays open-side down and hold the load through the full washer cycle.
steps.title: Load and run the washer-disinfector
steps.why: A washer-disinfector cycle is validated as a whole — spray pattern, detergent, temperature and time together — and opening the door partway through means none of it ran for as long as this load needed.

steps.cue: Read the cycle's printed temperature and commit once it's within the machine's own validated range.

gauge.label: WASH TEMP
gauge.missNote: That reading is outside the validated range — the load did not see what the cycle needed. Hold it for rewashing, not release.

steps.prompt: Read the cycle's printed temperature and commit once it's within the machine's own validated range.
steps.title: Verify the washer-disinfector's cycle parameters
steps.why: The washer's manufacturer instructions for use set the temperature and time the cycle has to actually reach for the mechanical wash to count — a cycle that finished without ever reaching that reading washed nothing, whatever the door light says.

steps.cue: Move the washed, dried tray through the pass-through window onto the assembly bench.

drag.missNote: Not on the assembly bench — the clean side is the only place a washed tray belongs.

steps.prompt: Move the washed, dried tray through the pass-through window onto the assembly bench.
steps.title: Pass the clean tray to the assembly side
steps.why: The pass-through window is the one controlled crossing between the dirty and clean sides — a tray only moves through it once it's actually washed and dried, never carried around the line by hand.

steps.cue: Verify every instrument's type and quantity against the tray's own count sheet.
steps.prompt: Verify every instrument's type and quantity against the tray's own count sheet.
steps.title: Count the tray against its count sheet
steps.why: A missing instrument found in this room is a missing instrument; a missing instrument found in a patient later is a retained surgical item — the count sheet is what catches the gap here, on the bench, instead of in the OR.

steps.cue: Two instruments on this tray are damaged, not dirty. Find them before assembly.

itemNames.broken-tip: an instrument with a broken tip

itemNotes.broken-tip: A broken tip is a functional failure, not a cleanliness problem — sterilizing it does not fix it, and it goes to repair, not back in the tray.
itemNotes.stained-instrument: Staining and pitting like this usually means the instrument's surface is already compromised — it gets pulled for evaluation rather than packaged and sent out to fail on the next case.

steps.prompt: Two instruments on this tray are damaged, not dirty. Find them before assembly.
steps.title: Function-test every instrument before it's packaged
steps.why: A washer and a sterilizer both act on whatever instrument is in front of them — neither one checks whether the instrument still works, which is why every piece gets looked at and tested by hand before it goes back into a tray.

steps.cue: Line the tray, arrange every instrument in the layout the count sheet shows, then place the internal indicator.

itemNames.arrange-tray: arrange instruments to the count sheet

steps.outOfOrderNote: Liner, then the instruments arranged to the sheet, then the indicator on top — the indicator only proves anything if it's actually inside the finished layout.
steps.prompt: Line the tray, arrange every instrument in the layout the count sheet shows, then place the internal indicator.
steps.title: Assemble the tray to its count sheet
steps.why: The layout on the count sheet exists so the surgical team can see at a glance that everything is present and undamaged the moment the tray opens — a tray assembled any other way makes the OR do the counting work all over again under time pressure.

steps.cue: Rotate the latch fully closed and confirm the seal.
steps.prompt: Rotate the latch fully closed and confirm the seal.
steps.title: Latch the rigid sterilization container
steps.why: A rigid container only keeps its contents sterile if its filter and gasket seal is actually engaged — a latch left half-turned looks closed but leaves a gap steam can get through on the way in and contamination can get through on the way out.

steps.cue: Start the cycle and stay with it until the chamber cycles through on its own.
steps.holdBreakNote: You broke off before the chamber finished its own cycle. Counting a shortened run as done is guessing that the missing minutes wouldn't have mattered.
steps.prompt: Start the cycle and stay with it until the chamber cycles through on its own.
steps.title: Run the sterilizer cycle
steps.why: Steam sterilization works by combining three numbers over the same span of minutes, not any one of them alone — a door popped open early trims all three at once, so the exposure this tray gets is whatever the shortened run happened to reach, not what the cycle was built to deliver.

steps.cue: Match the printed numbers against the sterilizer's posted spec before you sign off on this load.

gauge.label: CHAMBER TEMP
gauge.missNote: You signed off on a printout that never actually sat inside spec. Send the load back through rather than release it on a reading like that.

steps.prompt: Match the printed numbers against the sterilizer's posted spec before you sign off on this load.
steps.title: Read the sterilizer's printout
steps.why: AAMI ST79 makes the paper strip, not the indicator light, the record a load's release rests on — a chamber can flash "cycle complete" after a run that stalled below temperature the whole way through, and only the printed trace would ever show that.

steps.cue: Run the biological indicator with its matched control, then close out the load record.
steps.outOfOrderNote: Run the spore strip and its control before you touch the log — a record with no result behind it is just a blank line with a timestamp.
steps.prompt: Run the biological indicator with its matched control, then close out the load record.
steps.title: Run the biological indicator and log the load
steps.why: A chemical indicator only shows the chamber reached conditions; the spore strip is what actually gets exposed to those conditions and either dies or doesn't, and its matched control is the reason a clean result means the spores were alive to begin with rather than dead in the vial before the cycle ever ran. None of that protects a soul, though, until it's written down against a tray someone can find again.

supportLine: your employer's employee assistance program, or SEIU-UHW's member resources if a load like this one has you second-guessing the count
